character.centerRule: Peter remains the stable human center; parallel witnesses and later uses must stay attached to their own inspectable Scripture Scenes.

phases.orientation: Simon is introduced through family, fishing, a new name, a household, and appointment among the Twelve.
phases.title: Called and named

phases.orientation: Peter watches, speaks, asks, steps forward, is corrected, and follows through changing scenes in Galilee and Judea.
phases.title: Following and confessing

phases.orientation: Preparation, washing, questions, promises, warning, and predicted denial gather around the final meal.
phases.title: Table and warning

phases.orientation: Peter sleeps, draws a sword, follows, denies, weeps, and later runs toward reports of an empty tomb.
phases.title: Garden, denial, and tomb

phases.orientation: A catch, a meal, three questions, a commission, and a word about following reshape Peter’s place among the disciples.
phases.title: Breakfast and restoration

phases.orientation: Peter addresses the gathered disciples, speaks publicly, heals, answers authorities, and acts within the Jerusalem community.
phases.title: Witness in Jerusalem

character.throughline: Simon is named Peter while work, household, questions, confession, correction, fear, denial, restoration, speech, healing, conflict, travel, prison, mission, and later testimony gather around the same person.

leftEvidence.title: Simon and Andrew leave their nets after a direct summons

points.label: Setting and work
points.left: Casting and mending nets are named as Jesus passes beside the sea.
points.right: Empty boats, washed nets, teaching from Simon’s boat, and a second lowering fill the scene.

points.label: Response
points.left: The brothers immediately leave nets and follow.
points.right: Simon speaks twice, partners share the catch, fear is named, and all leave everything.

compares.posture: Read each calling sequence on its own terms before noticing shared people, work, and movement.

rightEvidence.title: Simon answers a command, sees the catch, and leaves everything

compares.tension: The two scenes place Peter’s following within different sequences without identifying one as a replacement for the other.
compares.title: Nets left / catch received

leftEvidence.title: Peter names Jesus and receives a far-reaching reply

points.label: Peter’s speech
points.left: Peter answers a question about Jesus’s identity.
points.right: Peter takes Jesus aside and rejects the announced outcome.

points.label: Jesus’s answer
points.left: Revelation, rock, assembly, and keys shape the response.
points.right: Stumbling, human concerns, cross, life, and following shape the response.

compares.posture: Keep the change of subject—from identity to suffering and following—visible.

rightEvidence.title: Peter rebukes the announced suffering and is redirected toward following

compares.tension: Peter’s affirmed confession and his immediate resistance stand next to one another in Matthew’s sequence.
compares.title: Confession / resistance

leftEvidence.title: Peter sees the transfiguration and hears the cloud’s command

points.label: Selected details
points.left: Clothing, Moses, Elijah, tents, cloud, voice, looking around, and descent are narrated.
points.right: Majesty, honor, glory, the beloved Son, the heard voice, and the holy mountain are selected.

points.label: Peter’s place
points.left: Peter speaks because he does not know what to say and shares the command to silence.
points.right: The writer speaks as an eyewitness opposing invented stories and preparing future remembrance.

compares.posture: Attribute narrative detail and later recollection to their separate sources.

rightEvidence.title: The letter recalls majesty, voice, Son, and holy mountain

compares.tension: The later letter omits Peter’s proposed tents while making the heard voice central to its eyewitness claim.
compares.title: Mountain witnessed / mountain remembered

leftEvidence.title: The Lord’s look stands between the crow and Peter’s remembered words

points.label: Recognition
points.left: Association, group identity, and Galilean origin are raised by three speakers.
points.right: Presence with Jesus, discipleship, and Galilean speech are raised by servant girls and bystanders.

points.label: Final turn
points.left: The Lord turns and looks at Peter before Peter remembers.
points.right: The rooster crows and Peter remembers the predicted denial.

compares.posture: Let parallel witness preserve difference in speaker, wording, and sequence.

rightEvidence.title: Oath, cursing, Galilean speech, crow, memory, and weeping intensify the sequence

compares.tension: Both accounts end in remembered words and bitter weeping while selecting different details around the final recognition.
compares.title: Two tellings of the denial

leftEvidence.title: Peter runs after the women speak and leaves wondering

points.label: Who reports
points.left: A group of women reports words remembered from the messengers.
points.right: Mary Magdalene reports that the Lord has been taken away.

points.label: At the tomb
points.left: Peter stoops, sees linen cloths, and departs wondering.
points.right: The two disciples arrive differently; Peter enters, sees cloths, and the beloved disciple sees and believes.

compares.posture: Do not merge the women’s reports or the two accounts of seeing.

rightEvidence.title: Peter and the beloved disciple run, enter, see, and return

compares.tension: The two reports preserve different messengers, companions, observations, and responses while placing Peter at the tomb.
compares.title: Peter runs / Peter enters

leftEvidence.title: Peter denies association three times and leaves weeping

points.label: Threefold speech
points.left: Three people identify Peter; he answers with denial each time.
points.right: Jesus questions Simon three times; Simon affirms affection each time.

points.label: Ending
points.left: Look, memory, departure, and weeping close the courtyard scene.
points.right: Commission, future death, and “Follow me” close the breakfast exchange.

compares.posture: Treat the relation as an authored comparison, not a declared equation in the passages themselves.

rightEvidence.title: Simon answers three questions and receives three commands to feed

compares.tension: The texts do not explicitly label the breakfast exchange as a reversal of the courtyard, yet the repeated threefold speech invites inspection.
compares.title: Three denials / three commissions

leftEvidence.title: Simon lowers the nets at Jesus’s word before leaving everything

points.label: Failed night and command
points.left: A fruitless night precedes a command to put out and lower nets.
points.right: A fruitless night precedes a shore-side command to cast on the right side.

points.label: Response after abundance
points.left: Simon falls before Jesus, names himself, hears reassurance, and leaves everything.
points.right: Peter jumps into the sea, helps draw the net ashore, and joins breakfast.

compares.posture: Observe repetition without treating the later scene as a word-for-word replay.

rightEvidence.title: Peter returns to fishing before recognizing Jesus on shore

compares.tension: Similar work, failure, command, and abundance surround two very different moments in Peter’s path.
compares.title: Catch at the call / catch after the tomb

leftEvidence.title: Peter redirects amazement from human power and speaks from Israel’s Scriptures

points.label: Audience question
points.left: Peter asks why the crowd marvels or stares at the apostles.
points.right: The rulers ask by what power or name the act was done.

points.label: Response to the healing
points.left: The speech moves through Jesus, ancestors, ignorance, repentance, prophets, and blessing.
points.right: The answer names Jesus, rejection, resurrection, cornerstone, salvation, and the healed man’s visible presence.

compares.posture: Keep audience, question, setting, and consequence visible.

rightEvidence.title: Peter answers a question about power and name under arrest

compares.tension: One healing generates both invitation to the public and conflict with authorities, with Peter adapting the account to each audience.
compares.title: Healing explained / healing defended

leftEvidence.title: Peter and John are questioned and ordered not to speak in Jesus’s name

points.label: Authority and command
points.left: Rulers interrogate the healing and command silence.
points.right: An angel commands public speech before the council repeats its prohibition.

points.label: Apostolic answer
points.left: Peter and John contrast human judgment with what they have seen and heard.
points.right: Peter and the apostles contrast obedience to God with human authority and identify themselves as witnesses.

compares.posture: Trace recurrence and escalation without flattening the two custody scenes.

rightEvidence.title: The apostles leave prison, teach again, and answer the high priest

compares.tension: The second scene repeats the prohibition after an opposing command has already returned the apostles to public teaching.
compares.title: First command to silence / renewed command to speak

leftEvidence.title: Peter enters, speaks, witnesses the Spirit, and commands baptism

points.label: Narrated sequence
points.left: Cornelius’s welcome, Peter’s threshold statement, speech, interruption, amazement, and baptism unfold.
points.right: Vision, three repetitions, visitors, six brothers, Cornelius’s angel report, Peter’s beginning, and remembered words are selected.

points.label: Conclusion
points.left: Peter asks whether water can be withheld after the Spirit is visibly received.
points.right: Peter asks who he was to withstand God after the same gift is given.

compares.posture: Let event and defense retain their distinct settings and purposes.

rightEvidence.title: Peter explains the sequence to critics and argues from the gift received

compares.tension: The retelling selects evidence needed for a Jerusalem dispute rather than repeating the Caesarea scene in full.
compares.title: House entered / event retold

leftEvidence.title: The Jerusalem group says the Lord has appeared to Simon

points.label: Immediate setting
points.left: The report is heard when the Emmaus travelers return to the Eleven and companions.
points.right: The appearance belongs to a received sequence of death, burial, resurrection, and witnesses.

points.label: What is supplied
points.left: Luke states the appearance without narrating its encounter.
points.right: Paul states appearance to Cephas and then expands the witness list without narrating the encounter.

compares.posture: Notice what both attest and what neither describes.

rightEvidence.title: Paul names Cephas first in a sequence of resurrection appearances

compares.tension: Both sources preserve the appearance as a statement while leaving the encounter itself unnarrated.
compares.title: Appeared to Simon / appeared to Cephas

leftEvidence.title: Cephas joins James and John in extending fellowship across missions

points.label: Relationship to Gentiles
points.left: The leaders recognize Paul’s entrusted mission and request remembrance of the poor.
points.right: Cephas’s earlier eating changes to withdrawal and separation.

points.label: Paul’s account
points.left: Paul narrates recognition, grace, pillars, right hands, and agreed fields of work.
points.right: Paul narrates opposition, fear, spread to others, judgment, and public address.

compares.posture: Do not import a resolution that Galatians does not narrate.

rightEvidence.title: Cephas withdraws from eating with Gentiles after others arrive

compares.tension: The same letter places recognized mission fellowship beside a later rupture in shared table practice.
compares.title: Fellowship extended / table fellowship withdrawn

leftEvidence.title: Jesus says Simon will be called Cephas, interpreted as Peter

points.label: Names
points.left: Simon, son of Jonah, Cephas, and Peter appear in one sentence.
points.right: Simon Peter appears with servant and apostle as the writer’s self-identification.

points.label: Forward movement
points.left: The new name is spoken before Peter’s narrated discipleship.
points.right: The opening looks toward calling, qualities, fruit, and future entry.

compares.posture: Keep narrative naming and epistolary self-presentation distinct.

rightEvidence.title: Simon Peter identifies himself as servant and apostle

compares.tension: The Gospel announces the name prospectively; the letter begins from the combined name and two roles.
compares.title: Name given / name used

leftEvidence.title: Peter argues from the Spirit’s gift and warns against placing a yoke

points.label: Gentile inclusion
points.left: Peter recalls Gentiles hearing, believing, receiving the Spirit, and having hearts purified.
points.right: Paul recalls Gentile table fellowship, withdrawal, and the effect on other Jews and Barnabas.

points.label: Public speech
points.left: Peter addresses assembled apostles and elders after much debate.
points.right: Paul says he addressed Cephas before everyone when conduct did not align with the gospel’s truth.

compares.posture: Avoid assuming a timeline or resolution beyond what these sources supply.

rightEvidence.title: Paul says Cephas withdrew from Gentile table fellowship under pressure

compares.tension: Peter’s public council argument and Paul’s account of Cephas’s public conduct pull attention to speech, action, and pressure in different settings.
compares.title: Council speech / Antioch confrontation

leftEvidence.title: Two pairs of brothers leave nets and boat as Jesus passes beside the sea

points.label: Opening frame
points.left: Jesus walks beside the Sea of Galilee and sees two brothers casting a net.
points.right: Jesus enters Galilee proclaiming after John is taken into custody, then sees Simon and Andrew casting a net.

points.label: Second pair
points.left: James and John leave the boat and their father when called.
points.right: James and John leave their father with the hired servants when called.

compares.posture: Let the parallel witnesses remain distinct while their shared sequence is inspected.

rightEvidence.title: The kingdom announcement precedes the summons to Simon and Andrew

compares.tension: Closely parallel calls preserve different opening frames and details around what the two pairs leave.
compares.title: Passing beside the sea / beginning in Galilee

leftEvidence.title: The fever is reported, Jesus takes her hand, and Simon later joins the search

points.label: Healing action
points.left: Jesus comes, takes her hand, raises her, and the fever leaves.
points.right: Jesus stands over her, rebukes the fever, and it leaves her.

points.label: Afterward
points.left: The city gathers at the door; after prayer Simon and companions search for Jesus.
points.right: Many are brought at sunset; after solitude the crowds seek to keep Jesus from leaving.

compares.posture: Keep each sequence and vocabulary attached to its own Gospel witness.

rightEvidence.title: Jesus rebukes the fever before the day widens into healing and proclamation

compares.tension: The witnesses preserve the same household relationship and immediate service while selecting different healing actions and seekers.
compares.title: Simon’s house in Mark / Simon’s house in Luke

leftEvidence.title: Testing, prayer, return, strengthening, confidence, and denial are spoken together

points.label: Peter’s claim
points.left: Simon says he is ready to go with Jesus both to prison and to death.
points.right: Peter asks why he cannot follow now and says he will lay down his life.

points.label: Jesus’s reply
points.left: Prayer, turning, strengthening, and denial before the rooster crows are named.
points.right: Present inability, later following, and denial before the rooster crows are named.

compares.posture: Compare the two table exchanges without combining their distinct promises or sequence.

rightEvidence.title: Peter asks about destination, promises his life, and hears that following is delayed

compares.tension: Both warnings place Peter’s confident claim beside predicted denial while framing what follows in different terms.
compares.title: Strengthen your brothers / follow afterward

leftEvidence.title: Peter enters with James and John while Jesus takes the child’s hand and speaks

points.label: Inside the room
points.left: Jesus permits Peter, James, John, and the child’s parents to enter.
points.right: Peter sends everyone out before kneeling and praying alone beside Tabitha.

points.label: Word and movement
points.left: Jesus takes the child’s hand and tells her to arise; she gets up and walks.
points.right: Peter turns to the body and tells Tabitha to arise; she opens her eyes, sits up, and is presented alive.

compares.posture: Observe verbal and spatial recurrence without making the two agents or scenes interchangeable.

rightEvidence.title: Peter sends everyone out, kneels, prays, turns to the body, and speaks

compares.tension: Peter first appears as a selected witness in a raising scene and later as the one who prays and addresses Tabitha.
compares.title: Witness inside the room / prayer inside the room

leftEvidence.title: Peter completes the speech, answers the crowd, and calls for baptism

points.label: Speech and response
points.left: The speech reaches its conclusion; hearers ask what to do and receive an answer.
points.right: The Holy Spirit falls while Peter is still speaking and the circumcised believers hear the nations speaking.

points.label: Baptism
points.left: Those receiving the word are baptized after repentance and promise are named.
points.right: Peter asks whether water can be forbidden and commands baptism after the Spirit’s arrival.

compares.posture: Keep Jerusalem and Caesarea, their audiences, and their narrated order distinct.

rightEvidence.title: The Spirit interrupts Peter’s speech before he commands baptism

compares.tension: Peter speaks about the Spirit and baptism in both settings, but the order of speech, visible gift, question, and baptism differs.
compares.title: Jerusalem hearers / Caesarea hearers

leftEvidence.title: Simon answers three questions and receives three commands about Jesus’s sheep

points.label: Shepherd language
points.left: Feed my lambs, tend my sheep, and feed my sheep answer Simon’s three replies.
points.right: Shepherd God’s flock, exercise oversight willingly, and become examples define the appeal.

points.label: Authority and following
points.left: The commission closes with a word about Peter’s death and the command to follow.
points.right: The appeal rejects domination and points toward the chief Shepherd’s appearance.

compares.posture: Distinguish the Gospel commission from the letter’s address to a plurality of elders.

rightEvidence.title: A fellow elder and witness directs elders in tending God’s flock

compares.tension: A personal commission about the flock stands beside a later appeal that frames shepherding as shared, willing, and exemplary work.
compares.title: Feed my sheep / shepherd the flock

leftEvidence.title: Jesus speaks of Peter’s old age and the death by which he would glorify God

points.label: Death and departure
points.left: Another will dress Peter and carry him where he does not wish to go; the narrator identifies death.
points.right: The writer says the tent will soon be put off and names Jesus as the one who made this known.

points.label: What follows
points.left: The explanation is followed by the command “Follow me.”
points.right: The anticipated departure is followed by work intended to preserve remembrance.

compares.posture: Keep narrative prediction and epistolary self-presentation distinct.

rightEvidence.title: The letter treats departure as imminent and prepares continuing remembrance

compares.tension: A narrated prediction of Peter’s death stands beside a letter’s self-presentation at the approach of departure.
compares.title: Death foretold / departure remembered

leftEvidence.title: The mountain scene begins “after six days”

points.label: Opening interval
points.left: Matthew says “after six days” before Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain.
points.right: Luke says “about eight days after these sayings” before Jesus takes Peter, John, and James up the mountain to pray.

points.label: Shared mountain witness
points.left: Peter proposes three tents after Moses and Elijah appear, and the cloud’s voice directs the disciples to Jesus.
points.right: Peter proposes three tents as Moses and Elijah depart, and the cloud’s voice directs the disciples to Jesus.

points.label: Descent and speech
points.left: Jesus addresses their fear and commands silence until the resurrection while they descend.
points.right: The disciples keep silent and tell no one in those days what they have seen.

compares.posture: Preserve each time marker and sequence without calculating a resolution the sources do not supply.

rightEvidence.title: The mountain scene begins “about eight days after these sayings”

compares.tension: The witnesses attach different approximate intervals and distinct surrounding details to recognizably parallel mountain scenes.
compares.title: After six days / about eight days

leftEvidence.title: Three denials unfold around two rooster crows while Jesus is before the council

points.label: Rooster sequence
points.left: A rooster crows after the first denial, then again after the third denial.
points.right: The rooster crows immediately after Peter’s third denial.

points.label: Words remembered
points.left: Peter remembers the prediction that before the rooster crows twice he will deny Jesus three times.
points.right: Peter remembers the prediction that before the rooster crows he will deny Jesus three times.

points.label: Final turn
points.left: Peter breaks down and weeps.
points.right: The Lord turns and looks at Peter before Peter goes outside and weeps bitterly.

compares.posture: Keep both narrated sequences inspectable without merging their selected details.

rightEvidence.title: Three denials are followed by a rooster crow, the Lord’s look, memory, and weeping

compares.tension: Mark and Luke preserve three denials and remembered prediction while narrating the rooster sequence and final turn differently.
compares.title: Twice in Mark / once in Luke
